title: Camera-style rotation and tap to focus
description: The phone's orientation, not the screen, decides whether a shot is portrait or landscape (the official sensor-plus-device rotation rule), and a tap on the picture focuses on that spot of the sensor.

clauses.text: The frame comes out upright for however the phone is held: back camera rotation = sensor + device angle, front camera = sensor - device angle (Android's JPEG-orientation rule).
clauses.observable_by: a test named "frames come out upright however the phone is held" passes

clauses.text: Tapping a spot on the picture focuses on that same spot of the camera sensor, for every rotation and with the picture cropped to 4:3 or 3:4.
clauses.observable_by: a test named "tap maps to the same spot on the sensor" passes

cases.description: sampleRotation for back and front cameras at device angles 0/90/180/270, including wrap-around
for rotations 0/90/180/270 and 4:3 and 3:4 crops, a bright block placed at sensorPoint(u, v) shows up at (u, v) of the sampled picture
